maturityDefinitions.candidate: Intended for the default developer-preview journey, but not publishable until every applicable P0 gate passes against one frozen commit and its final artifacts.
maturityDefinitions.experimental: Optional, opt-in functionality with explicitly limited support. It must not be required by the default journey.
maturityDefinitions.deferred: Implemented or partially implemented in source, but excluded from this release because required evidence or safety gates are incomplete.
maturityDefinitions.planned: Not included in the release and must not be described as currently usable.

audience: JavaScript and TypeScript developers who use an existing AI coding assistant
promise: A tested route to a private desktop app with local data, local AI, and direct peer communication.

steps: Install the exact preview CLI artifact.
Configure an assistant workspace with us init.
Scaffold a Pear Desktop app with local-ai.
Install and run the generated app from its own folder.
Make one visible change with the generated assistant instructions.
Verify local persistence and offline restart after the model is installed.
commands: us scaffold app -p pear-desktop -n coffee-assistant -f local-ai

limitations: The current init flow creates an assistant workspace, not a running app.
Final package installation from the intended public channel is not verified.
104 canonical and bundled files match; automatic drift checks apply to the candidate.
Recommended assistant path has not completed an independent pilot.

releaseScope.capability: Pear Desktop scaffold with local storage and P2P networking
limitations: The recorded test evidence used generated-app and worker checks; the final clean-machine journey remains unverified.
Frozen installed-artifact UI passed real completion, forced failure/retry, cancellation, post-cancel reuse and network-isolated restart with existing persisted data.
Cold download and interrupted transfer recovery passed on this Mac; other machines and broader resource limits remain unverified.
Mock mode is test support and is not a public demonstration.
Maintained source is frozen; repository remains private pending account administration.
Public DHT retrieval, visible graceful disconnection, persistence and fresh reconnect reads passed using distinct instances on one Mac.
Fresh screenshots and walkthrough show merged QVAC 0.21 source; independent reproduction remains pending.

verificationRuns.scope: Network-isolated generated Pear Desktop real-QVAC restart
verificationRuns.command: QVAC_REAL_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS=600000 npm run test:e2e:desktop:qvac:offline -- --skip-build
verificationRuns.details: macOS sandbox-exec denied every non-localhost network operation while leaving Playwright's localhost CDP connection available. The generated app reused the cached pinned model, recovered from the forced missing-local-model error, completed real inference, cancelled a long response through the SDK, and completed another prompt. Offline model-ready took 1.021 seconds and the full app process tree used 1,396.4 MiB RSS.
verificationRuns.note: Run on macOS arm64 against the dirty source build. This directly validates cached-model operation without external connectivity; cold first-run/download timing and a frozen-artifact repeat remain open.

verificationRuns.scope: Generated Pear Desktop real-QVAC cancellation and recovery
verificationRuns.command: QVAC_REAL_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS=600000 npm run test:e2e:desktop:qvac -- --skip-build
verificationRuns.details: The regenerated app first requested a deliberately missing local model and exposed the SDK error in the UI. Retry loaded the cached pinned model, completed an initial prompt, began streaming a deliberately long response, invoked sdk.cancel for the active inference through the Stop control, observed the stopped UI state, and completed a recovery prompt on the same loaded model. A repeat measured 1.026 seconds from Retry to warm model-ready and 1,464.7 MiB RSS across the complete generated-app process tree. Worker startup, storage integrity, and the full Electron UI flow passed in five seconds.
verificationRuns.note: Run on macOS arm64 against the dirty source build. The timing and RSS values describe this machine rather than a minimum requirement. Network-isolated restart, cold first-run/download timing, and the frozen release artifact remain unverified.
